relation_types.extends: refines or builds directly on the target theory
relation_types.rivals: offers a competing explanation of the same phenomenon
relation_types.complements: compatible; the two are often combined
relation_types.synthesizes: integrates the target with other theories
relation_types.applies: carries the target's logic to a new domain

theories.label: Classical realism
theories.core: States pursue power rooted in human nature; prudent statecraft manages the balance of power.

theories.label: Structural realism (neorealism)
theories.core: Anarchy and the distribution of capabilities make states balance; bipolarity is stable.

works.label: Waltz 1979
works.title: Theory of International Politics

theories.label: Defensive realism
theories.core: States seek security, not maximal power; the security dilemma and offense-defense balance shape conflict.

works.label: Jervis 1978
works.title: Cooperation under the Security Dilemma

theories.label: Offensive realism
theories.core: Anarchy pushes great powers to maximize relative power and seek regional hegemony.

works.label: Mearsheimer 2001
works.title: The Tragedy of Great Power Politics

theories.label: Balance of threat
theories.core: States balance against threats (power, proximity, offensive capability, intentions), not power alone.

works.label: Walt 1987
works.title: The Origins of Alliances

theories.label: Neoclassical realism
theories.core: Systemic pressures are filtered through domestic perceptions and state capacity.

theories.label: Power transition & hegemonic war
theories.core: War is most likely when a dissatisfied rising power approaches parity with the dominant state.

works.label: Gilpin 1981
works.title: War and Change in World Politics

theories.label: Hegemonic stability theory
theories.core: An open, stable order needs a hegemon to supply public goods.

works.label: Gilpin 1981
works.title: War and Change in World Politics

works.label: Keohane 1984
works.title: After Hegemony: Cooperation and Discord in the World Political Economy

theories.label: Neoliberal institutionalism
theories.core: Institutions enable cooperation under anarchy by reducing transaction costs and providing information.

works.label: Keohane 1984
works.title: After Hegemony: Cooperation and Discord in the World Political Economy

theories.label: Complex interdependence
theories.core: Multiple channels, no issue hierarchy and the low utility of force change world politics.

works.label: Keohane 1977
works.title: Power and Interdependence: World Politics in Transition
works.authors: Robert O. Keohane & Joseph S. Nye

theories.label: Regime theory
theories.core: Principles, norms, rules and procedures converge expectations in issue areas.

works.label: Krasner 1982
works.title: Structural Causes and Regime Consequences: Regimes as Intervening Variables

works.label: Ruggie 1982
works.title: International Regimes, Transactions, and Change: Embedded Liberalism in the Postwar Economic Order

theories.label: Rational design of institutions
theories.core: Institutional features such as membership, scope and flexibility are rational responses to cooperation problems.

works.label: Koremenos 2001
works.title: The Rational Design of International Institutions
works.authors: Barbara Koremenos, Charles Lipson & Duncan Snidal

theories.label: Principal-agent theory of IOs
theories.core: States delegate to IOs as principals; agency slack explains IO autonomy.

works.label: Hawkins 2006
works.title: Delegation and Agency in International Organizations
works.authors: Darren G. Hawkins, David A. Lake, Daniel L. Nielson & Michael J. Tierney (eds.)

works.label: Nielson 2003
works.title: Delegation to International Organizations: Agency Theory and World Bank Environmental Reform
works.authors: Daniel L. Nielson & Michael J. Tierney

theories.label: Compliance & screening
theories.origin: Chayes; Downs, Rocke & Barsoom; von Stein
theories.core: Treaties may change behavior or merely screen states already inclined to comply.

works.label: von Stein 2005
works.title: Do Treaties Constrain or Screen? Selection Bias and Treaty Compliance

works.label: Simmons 2009
works.title: Mobilizing for Human Rights: International Law in Domestic Politics

theories.label: Liberal theory (preferences first)
theories.core: State preferences, shaped by domestic society, drive world politics.

works.label: Moravcsik 1997
works.title: Taking Preferences Seriously: A Liberal Theory of International Politics

theories.label: Democratic peace
theories.core: Democracies rarely fight each other, through norms, institutions or information.

works.label: Tomz 2013
works.title: Public Opinion and the Democratic Peace
works.authors: Michael R. Tomz & Jessica L. P. Weeks

theories.label: Commercial & capitalist peace
theories.core: Trade, capital integration and development reduce conflict.

works.label: Gartzke 2007
works.title: The Capitalist Peace

theories.label: Two-level games
theories.core: Negotiators bargain simultaneously with foreign counterparts and domestic ratifiers.

works.label: Putnam 1988
works.title: Diplomacy and Domestic Politics: The Logic of Two-Level Games

theories.label: Bargaining model of war
theories.core: War is costly, so it requires private information, commitment problems or indivisibility.

works.label: Fearon 1995
works.title: Rationalist Explanations for War

works.label: Powell 2006
works.title: War as a Commitment Problem

theories.label: Audience costs
theories.core: Leaders who back down from public threats pay domestic costs, which makes threats credible.

works.label: Fearon 1994
works.title: Domestic Political Audiences and the Escalation of International Disputes

works.label: Tomz 2007
works.title: Reputation and International Cooperation: Sovereign Debt across Three Centuries

works.label: Weeks 2008
works.title: Autocratic Audience Costs: Regime Type and Signaling Resolve

theories.label: Constructivism
theories.core: Anarchy is what states make of it: identities and interests are socially constructed.

works.label: Wendt 1992
works.title: Anarchy is what States Make of it: The Social Construction of Power Politics

works.label: Wendt 1999
works.title: Social Theory of International Politics

theories.label: Norm life cycle
theories.core: Norms emerge through entrepreneurs, cascade and are internalized.

works.label: Finnemore 1998
works.title: International Norm Dynamics and Political Change

works.label: Keck 1998
works.title: Activists beyond Borders: Advocacy Networks in International Politics

theories.label: Socialization & persuasion
theories.core: IOs socialize states through persuasion, social influence and mimicry.

works.label: Johnston 2001
works.title: Treating International Institutions as Social Environments

theories.label: Securitization
theories.core: Issues become security issues through speech acts accepted by audiences.

theories.label: English School (international society)
theories.core: States form an international society with shared rules and institutions.

theories.label: Liberal international order
theories.core: Post-1945 U.S. hegemony built a rules-based order through strategic restraint and institutions.

works.label: Ikenberry 2001
works.title: After Victory: Institutions, Strategic Restraint, and the Rebuilding of Order after Major Wars

theories.label: Hierarchy in IR
theories.core: Relations among states are often hierarchical authority, not pure anarchy.

works.label: Lake 2009
works.title: Hierarchy in International Relations

theories.label: Weaponized interdependence
theories.core: States controlling network hubs can exploit panopticon and chokepoint effects.

works.label: Farrell 2019
works.title: Weaponized Interdependence: How Global Economic Networks Shape State Coercion
